newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates unchanged on fresh demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates unchanged on fresh demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates remained unchanged on Saturday on fresh demand from mill owners and are expected to maintain high levels as demand has exceeded supplies, dealers said.
"The arrival of fresh suplies has not picked up to match the mill owners' demand," dealer Kishan Chand said. "The arrival of fresh supplies will increase by the end of this month."
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety from the 1996/97 crop was traded at 2,400 rupees ($67.22) per maund (37.32 kg) and the MNH-93 at 2,450 to 2,500 rupees per maund, dealers said.
The Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said customs-cleared cotton exports had reached 1,824,676 375-lb bales by Aug 25, since the 1995/96 picking season began on September 1.
Imports had reached 47,545 480-lb bales in the same period.
